newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 picks Salt Lake City as site.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 picks Salt Lake City as site.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc, a huge manufacturer and direct marketer of personal computers, said Thursday it chose Salt Lake City, Utah, as the site for a $20 million manufacturing facility.

The new plant will sit on about 35 acres at Landmark at Salt Lake City, a planned industrial development. Construction is expected to begin this summer on the 260,000 square foot facility which will house the manufacturing operations, the company said in a news release.
Gateway 2000 will lease temporary manufacturing space nearby for about 200 initial employees until construction is completed on permanent headquarters in the late spring of 1998.

Gateway expects about 500 employees to be on the job shortly after the building is completed. Employment is projected to grow steadily over the next two to three years to eventually reach about 1,300 people.
The first PC is expected to be shipped before the end of 1997. In 1996, the company shipped 1.9 million systems and reported revenues of $5 billion.
